root_motivation: An agent that already presented its tenant key and then omits it on one call gets a second tenant, and its next keyed call cannot find the tool it just published -- two sessions did that today. The rule was documented (help.rs) and implemented per request (handler::implicit_signup_and_dispatch), but the connection's own earlier authenticated calls were never consulted, even though the schema already records which session created a tenant (tenants.created_session_id). This PRD binds implicit signup to a connection's first call and answers later key-less calls by naming the tenant the connection already is, by default refusing rather than silently creating (or silently reusing) a second one.
user_persona: Agent: forgets tenant_key on one call, receives tenant_key_missing with data.tenant naming its own tenant and a hint to pass that key, retries, and keeps its tools in one place. Operator (Joe): reads admin.funnel's new implicit_second_signup_blocked count and sees how many fragments the old behaviour would have created. Builder: runs the contract test that asserts a connection can create at most one tenant implicitly.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a fresh connection on bare /mcp, When the first host.tool_publish arrives without tenant_key, Then a tenant is created, the onboarding payload is returned, and created_session_id on the row is the connection's session id.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/sessbind_ac14_fresh_connection_implicit_signup_unchanged.rs -- a regression anchor proving implicit signup's existing first-call contract (PRD-mcphost-implicit-signup/PRD-mcphost-session-bound-tenant-after-signup) is unchanged by this PRD: one tenant created, onboarding.tenant matches the row, and tenants.created_session_id equals the server-issued Mcp-Session-Id.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given that same connection, When a second host.tool_publish arrives without tenant_key, Then no tenant is created, the response is tenant_key_missing with data.tenant equal to the first tenant's namespace and the hint naming it, and signup_events holds one implicit_second_signup_blocked row.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/sessbind_ac15_second_bare_call_is_refused_and_named.rs -- same session, second bare host.tool_publish: asserts the call errors tenant_key_missing with data.tenant/data.hint naming the first tenant, exactly one tenant row ever exists, and Db::count_implicit_second_signup_blocked reads back exactly one row.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a connection that authenticated with tenant A's key on one call, When a later call omits the key, Then the response is tenant_key_missing with data.tenant: "<A>" and no tenant is created; given reuse_session_tenant = true, Then the call runs as A with auth: "session".
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/sessbind_ac16_tenant_key_arg_then_omit_refused_or_reused.rs -- authenticates via the tenant_key argument (never the Authorization header, per resolve_tenant_key_auth's own single write site for AppState::tenant_key_arg_memory), then a key-less call on the same session: default refusal naming A, and (with AppState::reuse_session_tenant flipped true on the test server) the same key-less call instead succeeds as A with calls.auth_method == "session".

acceptance_criteria.description: Given two concurrent connections each without keys, When each makes its first call, Then two tenants are created with different created_session_ids, and neither connection's later key-less call creates a third.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/sessbind_ac17_concurrent_connections_isolated_memory.rs -- two independent session-continuity clients each implicitly sign up, asserts two distinct tenants with distinct created_session_id values, then a second key-less call on EITHER connection is refused (not a third signup), and exactly two tenants exist throughout.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a connection that signed up implicitly and then disconnects, When a new connection without a key calls, Then a new tenant is created (fresh client) and the old tenant is untouched.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/sessbind_ac18_reconnect_without_key_is_a_fresh_client.rs -- one session-continuity client implicitly signs up and is dropped (no continuity carried forward); a brand-new McpClient with no session, no header, no tenant_key calls bare and gets its OWN new tenant, while the first tenant's row (namespace, created_session_id) is read back unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given one blocked second signup today, When admin.funnel days=1 runs, Then it reports implicit_second_signup_blocked: 1; and host.whoami on the connection reports session_tenant.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/sessbind_ac19_funnel_blocked_count_and_whoami_session_tenant.rs -- triggers exactly one blocked second implicit signup, asserts admin.funnel({days:1}).implicit_second_signup_blocked == 1, then an authenticated host.whoami call on the same connection (over its own key) reports session_tenant equal to the connection's remembered tenant.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the docs build, When docs/ is regenerated, Then the reconnect rule appears under the one-URL onboarding section and help.rs's cause text names it.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/sessbind_ac20_docs_and_help_name_the_reconnect_rule.rs -- asserts docs/agent-quickstart.md's one-URL onboarding section names the reconnect/no-second-tenant rule, and help.rs's tenant_key_missing cause text mentions a connection that already named a tenant.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given prod mcphost.dev after deploy, When the next truth-tier panel runs, Then no session's ledger shows two distinct tenants created from one connection and admin.funnel shows a non-zero implicit_second_signup_blocked or zero with zero key-less second calls (Live; evidence: truth-tier session ledgers and admin.funnel of the first nightly after deploy).
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned: AC8's Then is a live, post-deploy observation on prod mcphost.dev (the next nightly truth-tier panel and admin.funnel reading). This dispatch has no prod deploy rights and no live truth-tier panel to observe; AC1-AC6 already prove the refuse-and-name/reuse mechanism itself end-to-end against an in-process server.

scope: src/state.rs: AppState gains implicit_signup_memory/tenant_key_arg_memory (crate::session_bind::SessionBindings, separate from the pre-existing session_bindings explicit-signup/redeem map) and reuse_session_tenant (Arc<AtomicBool>, default false -- parse_reuse_session_tenant/reuse_session_tenant_from_env reads $MCPHOST_IMPLICIT_SIGNUP_REUSE_SESSION_TENANT).

src/handler.rs: resolve_tenant_key_auth's own call site writes tenant_key_arg_memory on a successful tenant_key-argument auth (requirement 1); implicit_signup_and_dispatch's binding step is replaced by the new record_implicit_signup_memory (binds implicit_signup_memory, keeps created_session_id/notify_tool_list_changed, never touches state.session_bindings); a new consultation block in call_tool (after the existing session-binding check, before the invite-join check and the implicit-signup match arm) looks up both memories and either refuses-and-names (default; AppError::TenantKeyMissing(Some(namespace)), records implicit_second_signup_blocked only for the implicit-signup source) or reuses (reuse_session_tenant == true; auth_method/calls.auth_method "session", via reusing the pre-existing via_session_binding flag); the implicit-signup onboarding note names the new rule (P2).
src/errors.rs: AppError::TenantKeyMissing gains an Option<String> payload (the named tenant's namespace); into_error_data_at adds data.tenant/data.hint when Some.

src/db.rs: migration 0079 (signup_events.kind, default 'signup'); record_blocked_implicit_second_signup/count_implicit_second_signup_blocked; signup_count_since/try_admit_signup's own rate-limit queries gain AND kind = 'signup' so a blocked attempt never counts against the real signup rate limit.
src/admin.rs: admin::funnel gains implicit_second_signup_blocked (additive, same since_unix window as every other field).
src/control.rs: whoami gains session_tenant (the connection's remembered tenant's namespace, when either memory holds one) for AC6.

docs/agent-quickstart.md, src/help.rs: the reconnect rule (a key-less call on a connection that already named a tenant is refused and named, not re-signed-up) documented under the one-URL onboarding section and named in tenant_key_missing's cause text (AC7).
src/main.rs, src/enduser.rs, src/tables.rs, tests/common/mod.rs: every AppState literal updated for the three new fields.

tests/sessbind_ac1[4-9].rs, tests/sessbind_ac20.rs (new, one per non-deferred AC); tests/implsign_ac01*.rs, tests/implsign_ac02*.rs, tests/sessbind_ac08*.rs, tests/ownmt_ac01*.rs (updated: each asserted the pre-this-PRD default of silently reusing an implicit signup's binding on a later key-less call, which requirement 2 now supersedes with refuse-and-name).
agent/test-map.json: ac_test_map repointed at this PRD's ACs; the prior PRD's (mcphost-tool-call-host-verb-forward) map archived under ac_test_map_by_prefix.verbfwd.
non_goals: Changing the first-call experience for a fresh client (PRD's own Non-goals) -- AC1 is a regression anchor, not a behavior change.
Cross-connection memory -- a client reconnecting without a key is a fresh client; its personal /u/<secret>/mcp URL is the durable credential (PRD's own Non-goals; AC5).

Changing the pre-existing explicit signup/redeem session-binding mechanism (PRD-mcphost-session-bound-tenant-after-signup) -- that map (state.session_bindings) and its own unconditional reuse are untouched; this PRD's refuse-and-name default applies only to the connection memory it adds (implicit signup, and a successful tenant_key-argument auth).
AC8 (the live, deployed-server, prod truth-tier observation) -- operator-provisioned, deferred; needs a real prod deploy and the next nightly panel, neither of which this coder dispatch can produce.

additional.two_separate_memories_not_one_shared_wit: The PRD's own requirement 1 describes ONE piece of per-session state ("the tenant id of the most recent successful tenant_key auth and of an implicit signup it performed"), but the pre-existing state.session_bindings map (PRD-mcphost-session-bound-tenant-after-signup) already serves an overlapping role for explicit signup/redeem, with its own, DIFFERENT, unconditional-reuse consultation (resolve_session_binding) that several already-landed tests (sessbind_ac01-13) pin verbatim. Writing this PRD's new sources into that SAME map would either break those tests' own silent-reuse assertions or require threading provenance through a type that has none. Two new, separate AppState fields (implicit_signup_memory, tenant_key_arg_memory) -- same bounded/LRU/TTL SessionBindings type, zero changes to session_bind.rs itself -- keep the pre-existing mechanism's own tests green while giving this PRD's new refuse-and-name default (requirement 2) its own, independently-consulted state.
additional.implicit_signup_and_dispatch_no_longer_c: Before this PRD, implicit_signup_and_dispatch reused bind_session_to_created_tenant verbatim, which wrote into state.session_bindings -- meaning a second key-less call on an implicitly-signed-up connection was ALREADY being silently served as that tenant (via resolve_session_binding), exactly the behavior AC2 now supersedes. This PRD's own pre-existing-test fallout (implsign_ac01, implsign_ac02, sessbind_ac08's real_signups_land_in_the_running_servers_own_map, ownmt_ac01's implicit_first_call_carries_claim_url) is the direct, necessary consequence of that intentional default change, not a regression -- each was updated in place to read its own AC's surviving Then over the tenant's own /u/ URL (its real credential) instead of the now-refused key-less continuation.
additional.the_blocked_event_must_never_count_again: signup_events is also the real-signup rate-limit ledger (Db::signup_count_since/try_admit_signup, scoped by source_ip). A blocked second implicit signup creates no tenant and must not consume that same per-IP budget, so record_blocked_implicit_second_signup writes a dedicated kind ('implicit_second_signup_blocked') via its own plain INSERT -- never through try_admit_signup -- and the two rate-limit queries gained an explicit AND kind = 'signup' filter (migration 0079's own column default) so every pre-existing row's count is unchanged and only the new kind is excluded.
additional.via_session_binding_is_reused_not_a_new_: AC3's "runs as A with auth: session" is the SAME calls.auth_method value calls_auth_method already emits for the pre-existing session-binding reuse path (None if via_session_binding => "session") -- reusing that exact flag for this PRD's own reuse_session_tenant == true branch (rather than inventing a second bool threaded through calls_auth_method/maybe_attach_welcome_back) keeps that downstream labeling and the welcome_back eligibility gate consistent for every connection-level-trust call, old mechanism or new.
additional.reuse_session_tenant_is_an_arc_atomicboo: AppState derives Clone and is otherwise cheap to clone (every mutable field is already Arc-wrapped or itself cheaply-Clone, e.g. checkout_sessions/session_bindings). A plain bool read from $MCPHOST_IMPLICIT_SIGNUP_REUSE_SESSION_TENANT at startup can't be flipped per-test without threading a new parameter through the test harness's five-layer start_full_with_* builder chain (the established 'field, not env var, since tests run in parallel in one binary' convention already used for signup_rate_limit_per_hour etc.) -- an Arc<AtomicBool> lets AC3's own test flip it after TestServer::start() with a single .store() call instead.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does an agent that already has a key get a SECOND tenant just by omitting it once, when the schema already records which session created the first one?
five_whys_trace.a: The PRD's own problem statement says so directly: resolve_tenant_key_auth (the tenant_key-argument path) learns a successful key per-request and forgets it immediately -- nothing before this PRD ever wrote that success into any session-scoped memory, so the very next key-less call on the same connection looks identical to a genuinely fresh one and implicit_signup_and_dispatch mints a new tenant for it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not just make implicit signup's own existing session binding (state.session_bindings) answer a second key-less call by reusing the tenant, the way explicit signup/redeem already does?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 2's own 'Default: refuse-and-name' answers this directly -- Joe's own open question ('refuse-and-name (default) or serve-as-session-tenant?') was resolved toward refusal: a silent reuse is exactly the kind of connection-level trust the TL;DR's own grounding (five-whys chain B, 'the first minute still breaks three ways') flags as a case nobody designed for, so the safer default names the tenant and makes the agent pass its own key back, while reuse_session_tenant stays available for an operator who prefers the old silent behavior.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the refusal need to COUNT (signup_events/implicit_second_signup_blocked) instead of just returning an error?
five_whys_trace.a: The PRD's own success metrics table names it directly: 'implicit_second_signup_blocked per day: not measured -> > 0 and reported', the same visibility goal ('The orphan rate is visible') the Goals section states -- without a count, Joe has no way to tell a connection that quietly stopped retrying after one refusal from the dozens of fragmented signups prod was producing before this PRD.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the implicit-signup memory have to be a SEPARATE map from the pre-existing session_bindings, instead of just adding provenance to that one?
five_whys_trace.a: state.session_bindings' own consultation point (resolve_session_binding) is unconditional trust, and several already-landed tests (sessbind_ac01-13) pin that unconditional behavior verbatim for explicit signup/redeem -- adding a provenance field to the SAME map would still require resolve_session_binding itself to branch on it, which is the same code-shape as two maps with two different consultation functions, just with an extra enum tag threaded through a type (session_bind.rs) this PRD has no other reason to touch at all.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does host.whoami need a session_tenant field (AC6) when the refusal itself already names the tenant in data.tenant?
five_whys_trace.a: The refusal only fires on a REFUSED call -- an agent that successfully authenticates some other way (its own key, the header, the /u/ URL) on a connection that ALSO has memory of an earlier implicit signup or tenant_key-argument auth has no way to see that connection-level fact at all otherwise; AC6's own Then ('host.whoami on the connection reports session_tenant') is exactly that visibility, read independently of whichever credential the whoami call itself happened to authenticate with.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does the transport expose a session id the handler can read, or is this connection-scoped only (PRD's own Open question, owner: builder, due: at build)?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Yes -- handler::session_id(parts) already reads the server-minted Mcp-Session-Id crate::session_bind::RequestSessionId carries in the request's own extensions (the same identifier PRD-mcphost-session-bound-tenant-after-signup's own state.session_bindings already keys on), so this PRD's two new memories key on that exact same session id, not a raw connection handle.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Refuse-and-name (default) or serve-as-session-tenant (PRD's own Open question, owner: Joe, due: at build)?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Refuse-and-name by default, per requirement 2's own explicit statement; reuse_session_tenant (default false) serves as the session tenant instead when an operator sets it. See hard_constraints.reuse_session_tenant_is_an_arc_atomicbool_not_a_plain_bool.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does implicit signup's own pre-existing session binding (which silently let a second key-less call ride the first implicit tenant) stay, get removed, or move to a separate memory?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Moves to a separate memory (implicit_signup_memory) with its own refuse-and-name default consultation; state.session_bindings (explicit signup/redeem) is untouched. See hard_constraints.two_separate_memories_not_one_shared_with_the_pre_existing_session_bindings_map and .implicit_signup_and_dispatch_no_longer_calls_bind_session_to_created_tenant.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does a blocked second implicit signup's own signup_events row count against that source IP's real signup rate limit?
